author_or_org: MIT NANDA (Aditya Challapally, Chris Pease, Ramesh Raskar, Pradyumna Chari)

claims.question: q5
claims.claim: The report states that despite $30–40 billion in enterprise GenAI investment, 95% of organizations are getting zero return.
claims.quote: Despite $30 –40 billion in enterprise investment into GenAI, this report uncovers a surprising result in that 95% of organizations are getting zero return.

claims.question: q5
claims.claim: Only 5% of integrated AI pilots are extracting millions in value, while the vast majority have no measurable P&L impact.
claims.quote: Just 5% of integrated AI pilots are extracting millions in value, while the vast majority remain stuck with no measurable P&L impact.

claims.question: q5
claims.claim: Sixty percent of organizations evaluated enterprise-grade AI tools, but only 20 percent reached pilot stage and 5 percent reached production; most fail due to brittle workflows, lack of contextual learning, and misalignment with operations.
claims.quote: Sixty percent of organizations evaluated such tools, but only 20 percent reached pilot stage and just 5 percent reached production. Most fail due to brittle workflows, lack of contextual learning, and misalignment with day-to-day operations.

claims.question: q5
claims.claim: The core barrier to scaling is learning, not infrastructure, regulation, or talent; most GenAI systems do not retain feedback, adapt to context, or improve over time.
claims.quote: The core barrier to scaling is not infrastructure, regulation, or talent. It is learning. Most GenAI systems do not retain feedback, adapt to context, or improve over time.

claims.question: q5
claims.claim: External partnerships have twice the success rate of internal builds.
claims.quote: Implementation advantage : External partnerships see twice the success rate of internal builds

claims.question: q5
claims.claim: Successful buyers demand process-specific customization and evaluate tools based on business outcomes rather than software benchmarks.
claims.quote: Buyers who succeed demand process-specific customization and evaluate tools based on business outcomes rather than software benchmarks.

claims.question: q5
claims.claim: Users are skeptical of custom or vendor-pitched AI tools, describing them as brittle, overengineered, or misaligned with actual workflows.
claims.quote: Yet the same users were overwhelmingly skeptical of custom or vendor-pitched AI tools, describing them as brittle, overengineered, or misaligned with actual workflows.
